chunks: Ali, from his father, who narrated from his father, said:

I saw Abdullah ibn Jundab in the standing place (of Arafat), and I did not see a standing place that was better than his standing. He continued extending his hands to the sky, and his tears were flowing upon his cheeks until they reached the ground. So when the people dispersed, I said to him, 'O Abu Muhammad, I have not seen any standing place that was better than your standing.'

He said, 'By Allah, I did not supplicate except for my brethren. And that is because Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) informed me that whoever supplicates for his brother in his absence, a call is made from the Throne: 'And for you is a hundred thousand times [the reward].' So I disliked that I should leave a guaranteed hundred thousand for one [supplication] which I do not know whether it will be answered or not.'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The standing place, specifically referring to Arafat during Hajj
key_terms.بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ: In his absence; when the person is not present

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for supplicating for a brother in his absence according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on intercessory supplication (du'a) for the righteous, rooted in the teachings of Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS). It illustrates the theological principle that praying for a brother behind one's back yields a guaranteed, multiplied reward, prioritizing communal spiritual benefit over uncertain personal gains. This narrative underscores the value of selflessness and the efficacy of collective prayer in Shia devotional practice.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father who said,

‘I saw Abdullah Bin Jundab in the pausing stop (at Arafaat during Hajj), so I had not seen a pausing which was better than his pausing. He did not cease extending his hands towards the sky, and his tears were flowing upon his cheeks to the extent that they reached the ground. So when the people dispersed, I said to him, ‘O Abu Muhammad! I have not see such a pausing better than your pausing at all’.

He said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I did not supplicate except for my brethren, and that is because Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> informed me that the one who supplicates for his brother in his absence, a Call would come from the Throne: “And for you is the like of a hundred thousand multiple”. Therefore, I disliked that I should leave the guaranteed one hundred thousand for the sake of one which I do not know whether it would be Answered or not’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali has narrated from his father who has said the following:

“Once I saw ‘Abd Allah ibn Jundab in ‘Arafat but I had not seen any stay (spending the ninth day of Dulhajj) in ‘Arafat better than that. He continued stretching his hands to the sky and his tears flow on his both cheeks all the way to the ground. When people left I said to him, ‘O abu Muhammad, I have never seen a wonderful performance in ‘Arafat such as yours.’

He said, ‘By Allah I did not pray for anything but for my brothers (in belief) and that is because of abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) who told me that whoever prays for his brothers (in belief) in his absence is called from the Throne, ‘(O servant of Allah) you will have one hundred thousand times as much reward as one may for his prayer receive,’ thus, I did not like to leave one hundred thousand guaranteed for only one of mine, of which I am uncertain whether it is accepted or not.’”
